description:
FILED s400, from the #348 measurement.  NOT visible on main today: s400 landed
only the machine-portability half of #207, so closure.t's child still runs real
perl and the matrix still passes by construction.  It is one of the two holes
holding #348.

op/closure.t builds a matrix of closure cases, runs it in a CHILD interpreter
and checks the output.  WITH which_perl -> $PCLPERL the child runs PCL and the
file goes 267/3 -> 235/27; the sweep's copy, perl-tests/closure.t, goes
OK 272/0 -> PARTIAL 240/28 (it stops early -- child exit 65280 -- so ten rows
never run) and takes 64 s.

The failures are ONE family, and the compiler already announces it:

    Parser2 TODO: lexical 'foreach' possibly captured by nested sub named_57

i.e. a NAMED sub declared inside an ANON sub, closing over the enclosing
foreach (or filescope) variable.  Every "named in_anon foreach <slot>" row
(sub_scalar, sub_array, sub_hash, global_*, fs_*, foreach) gets undef where
perl gets the captured value; the "named filescope foreach <slot>" rows report
(missing) because the child stops; 2 x "exited cleanly" and 2 x "STDERR is
silent" are the child dying and the TODO message reaching stderr.

This is the gap CLAUDE.md's TODO section has carried since session 63 ("for my
$n (0..4) { sub { $n } } requires pl-foreach to create a new binding per
iteration"), now with a 24-row measurement behind it.  Pl/t/closure-01.t is
the unit-level guard to extend.


CLOSED s405 (b0fb372): one missing `next` in _hoist_nested_sub — a PROMOTED lexical is legitimately captured, the exemption its sibling scan _check_sub_captures has had since W5.  op/closure.t under PCL children 235/27 -> 267/3.

s407 NOTE: #337's shape 10 (`for my $i (1,2) { my sub g { "g$i" } g() }`) is the
same residue as this task's registered "will not stay shared" family â the
per-call-cell fix lifts both.  Sized separately from #337's rename half.
subject: closure.t: a NAMED sub inside an ANON sub does not capture the enclosing foreach/filescope variable (24 rows, measured s400; blocks #348)
